title: The Erdos n^2/25 max-cut conjecture for small multiples of five, via a per-root-MaxCut envelope and blow-up integrality
summary: Erdős conjectured that every triangle-free graph on $N$ vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most $N^2/25$ edges; the bound would be sharp, attained by the balanced blow-up $C_5[N/5]$. Writing $β(G)$ for the minimum number of edges whose deletion makes $G$ bipartite and $a(N) = \max\{β(G):G$ triangle-free on $N$ vertices$\}$, the conjecture is $a(N)\le N^2/25$, and for $N=5n$ it reads $a(5n)\le n^2$.
